arms.better: tm reached `source/utils/body.ts` directly from the issue's root-cause detail and made the intended flush-path change, but it reread that source repeatedly and stopped when the provider returned HTTP 429. The final message surfaced the raw rate-limit response and suggested `tm ticket retry T-1`, but offered no bounded in-run recovery or indication that waiting could help; it also never ran a test or submitted verification evidence. The independently applied regression tests passed for all 19 stream tests and the Chromium empty-response browser test, but the full browser test file failed because Firefox and WebKit executables are unavailable. A short, visible retry honoring provider timing, less repeated context, and a final status that separates the retained source edit from unverified work would make the run substantially more recoverable and clearer to the user.

OpenCode stated a scoped plan, found the `flush()` implementation, changed it to always emit the completion event with an empty chunk, added a focused regression test, and reported the successful 18-test stream run accurately. It recovered from several unsuccessful file reads caused by a misspelled path, which added navigation churn and context; resolving file paths from the tool's known working directory before repeating reads would make the run more efficient. The merged stream tests (19 tests) and the Chromium empty-response browser test passed, but the full browser test file exited nonzero because Firefox and WebKit executables are unavailable in the environment.
